title: Recorded Vein Diameter and Energy Allocation During Multitruncal Endovenous Laser Ablation
content: Background/Objectives: We examined whether lower linear endovenous energy density (LEED) in the anterior saphenous vein (ASV) was proportional to its smaller diameter during simultaneous great saphenous vein (GSV) and ASV ablation. Methods: This exploratory retrospective study used 136 procedural records from a 433-patient source cohort. The primary comparison included 56 ipsilateral GSV–ASV pairs from 46 procedures. Nominal endovenous fluence equivalent (EFE) was calculated from LEED and pre-tumescence diameter measured with patients recumbent. Bilateral log ratios were averaged within procedures. Patient-linked clinical outcomes were not analyzed. Results: Procedure-weighted ASV/GSV ratios were 0.58 for diameter (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.55–0.62), 0.75 for LEED (95% CI, 0.70–0.80), and 1.29 for nominal EFE (95% CI, 1.19–1.40). Lower ASV LEED with higher nominal EFE occurred in 39 of 56 limbs. The between-wavelength EFE-ratio contrast was 0.97 (95% CI, 0.82–1.15). Excluding ambiguous records yielded an EFE ratio of 1.27 (95% CI, 1.17–1.39). Conclusions: The reduction in ASV LEED was smaller than the reduction in recorded diameter. Reporting measurement conditions alongside diameter and LEED improves dosimetric interpretation. These findings do not establish optimal dosing or clinical benefit.
